nodes.label: Option A: keep bash, patch per incident (do nothing / buy)

nodes.rationale: Rejected: keeps non-portable sed -i, the read -n 1 -s CI lock and fragile ls -1 implicit ordering; each incremental patch becomes an excuse to never attack the root problem, so maintenance debt grows monotonically with the number of snippets.

nodes.label: Option B: SnippetComposer.groovy + gmaven 2.1.1 in process-resources
nodes.norm_label: option b: snippetcomposer.groovy + gmaven 2.1.1 in process-resources

nodes.norm_label: strategic directive: eliminate bash pre-processing ('futuro bem breve')

nodes.label: JSON contract precedence rule (contract beats LLM; out-of-contract proposals discarded)
nodes.norm_label: json contract precedence rule (contract beats llm; out-of-contract proposals discarded)
nodes.rationale: Decided at intake: the JSON contract takes precedence over LLM inference, and flags proposed by the LLM that are absent from the contract are discarded (silenced) with the archetype default applied.

nodes.label: Option A: single prompt emits the full mvn archetype:generate line
nodes.norm_label: option a: single prompt emits the full mvn archetype:generate line
nodes.rationale: Rejected: a hallucinated flag or type fails mvn archetype:generate at runtime with a confusing message, and output is not reproducible between runs - costs that get expensive later.

nodes.label: Option B (recommended): LLM proposes mapping, deterministic validator applies catalog defaults
nodes.norm_label: option b (recommended): llm proposes mapping, deterministic validator applies catalog defaults
nodes.rationale: Only option covering all 6 goals at once: the validator gives fail-fast against LLM flag hallucination, reproducibility via temperature 0 plus a deterministic cache, defaults applied by code rather than the LLM, and the JSON contract gets a formal place with explicit fail-fast.

nodes.label: Option C: keep bash_script/ (do-nothing baseline)
nodes.rationale: Baseline confirming B is worth the investment: none of the 6 goals is met, the JSON contract stays implicit, and the 10-step per-flag ritual documented in README.md keeps growing the bash_script/ directory.

nodes.label: Triple pain: bash maintenance + repetitive prompting + no formal contract
nodes.norm_label: triple pain: bash maintenance + repetitive prompting + no formal contract
nodes.rationale: The pain is triple: operational (keeping ~28 bash scripts synchronized per new flag), cognitive (answering the same prompts on every generation), architectural (the module's JSON contract exists only implicitly, scattered across terminal prompts and ad-hoc flags).

nodes.label: Deterministic contract-to-entity derivation rules (type from value, java.lang-only, strict Tipo:nome format)
nodes.norm_label: deterministic contract-to-entity derivation rules (type from value, java.lang-only, strict tipo:nome format)
nodes.rationale: Everything deterministic (reading attributes in map or list form, estimating the Java type from the JSON value, assembling the strict Tipo:nome list, forcing enable_custom_entity_attributes) moves into the mechanism; the LLM only estimates the entity name. Types are restricted to java.lang because the entity template emits no import for attribute types - anything else produces a project that does not compile.

nodes.label: FR-009 allowlist relaxation (entity_name accepted without literal contract key)
nodes.norm_label: fr-009 allowlist relaxation (entity_name accepted without literal contract key)
nodes.rationale: A minimal explicit allowlist (entity_name, optionally entity_package_name) lets an INFERENCE proposal pass without a literal contract key, provided the value matches the catalog validationRegex; all other flags keep the strict gate, and allowlisted keys must not appear in the discarded-proposals section.

nodes.label: FR-009 literal contract-key gate (root cause of inert contract)
nodes.norm_label: fr-009 literal contract-key gate (root cause of inert contract)
nodes.rationale: The gate assumes contract vocabulary coincides with flag vocabulary; a domain contract (entityName, attributes[]) never contains entity_name or custom_entity_attributes_list keys, so every LLM proposal derived from the contract is discarded - result: 0 CONTRACT / 0 INFERENCE / 32 DEFAULT, the declared 'fonte da verdade' contract is inert.

nodes.label: FR-017 / Principle V: contract content must not persist to version control
nodes.norm_label: fr-017 / principle v: contract content must not persist to version control
nodes.rationale: The contract may carry sensitive business data, so only the cache-key hash may be persisted; Metade C collides frontally with this rule if the raw contract is persisted into the (versioned) generated project - hence the derived-snapshot recommendation, later superseded when the maintainer chose the raw contract and the FR was explicitly amended.

nodes.label: Catalog fingerprint in cache key (SHA-256 over key+default+regex; legacy entries unreachable)
nodes.norm_label: catalog fingerprint in cache key (sha-256 over key+default+regex; legacy entries unreachable)
nodes.rationale: The cache key gains a catalog fingerprint so entries recorded before the flag removal become unreachable without migration - legacy lines would otherwise keep serving obsolete -Dabsolute_path_jsonfile_contract values pointing at empty paths with silent copyFile failure.

nodes.label: FR-018 non-empty defaultValue gate (exit code 4; mechanism 100% inoperant)
nodes.norm_label: fr-018 non-empty defaultvalue gate (exit code 4; mechanism 100% inoperant)
nodes.rationale: Every requiredProperty must have a non-empty defaultValue; the two empty defaults (entity_package_name and absolute_path_jsonfile_contract) aborted the whole mechanism with exit code 4 before any inference - the flag was literally inoperant and the mechanism 100% out of operation.

nodes.label: cacheLookup StackOverflowError - recursive Pattern$Loop regex over provenance report
nodes.norm_label: cachelookup stackoverflowerror - recursive pattern$loop regex over provenance report
nodes.rationale: cacheLookup validates each cache.jsonl line with a greedy star over an alternation group, which java.util.regex compiles as a recursive Pattern$Loop with one stack frame per character; the real provenance report (~1965 chars) exceeds the measured ~1726-char threshold, so every repeated invocation exits 1 and one poisoned line invalidates the whole cache for all inputs. Latent while the FR-018 gate aborted before the cache lookup; fixed later by parsing with JsonSlurper since the on-disk format was already valid JSON.

nodes.label: Fixture (integration test matrix)
nodes.rationale: The directory IS the matrix: a fixture is a self-contained scenario of flag values in its own subdirectory under src/test/resources/projects/, with archetype.properties as the source of truth — no central config to maintain, adding a scenario means adding a directory.

nodes.label: Integration Test Matrix for eda-archetype
nodes.rationale: Curated, not exhaustive: the maintainer prioritizes coverage and simplicity over speed; built on the standard maven-archetype-plugin integration-test goal — the same mechanism Apache uses for its own archetype — rather than a custom JUnit harness (rejected as reinventing the wheel, high cost, low value).

nodes.label: User Story 1: Baseline Smoke Coverage (minimal)
nodes.rationale: Without a baseline run every other comparison is meaningless; minimal is the cheapest end-to-end run and the regression-safe floor below which the archetype is broken.

nodes.label: User Story 2: Stress Coverage of Co-Enabled Flags (full)
nodes.norm_label: user story 2: stress coverage of co-enabled flags (full)
nodes.rationale: Co-enabled flags are the second-most likely place for the post-processor to misbehave (conditional branches interact); full is the cheapest way to exercise the stress surface — without it every individual flag looks fine but combinations blow up.

nodes.label: User Story 4: Binding Properties Coverage (per sub-module)
nodes.norm_label: user story 4: binding properties coverage (per sub-module)
nodes.rationale: Binding properties is a large multi-flag surface (one parent + 5 sub-flags); the Constitution requires immutable and mutable variants tested independently — this story is what makes that auditable (Principle IV).

nodes.label: Binding-properties sub-fixtures (external-binding-{default,list,map,mutable,validated}-only)
nodes.rationale: One fixture per binding-properties sub-module so each binding variant is exercised independently; external-binding-validated-only requires enable_default_binding_external_properties=true per the DEPENDS_ON rule in property-binding-properties.xml.

nodes.label: Specification Quality Checklist (001)
nodes.rationale: Validates spec completeness before planning; all items passed on first iteration with 0 NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers, so no user clarification round was required before /speckit.clarify or /speckit.plan.

nodes.label: Quickstart: end-to-end matrix validation guide
nodes.rationale: Focuses on the end-to-end validation flow; implementation details live in the spec and plan — the living matrix (flags under test and what each verify.groovy asserts) lives in src/test/resources/projects/README.md and is kept honest by FixturesMatrixTest.groovy rather than duplicated here.

nodes.label: Constitution Principle I: Modularidade por Chave de Ativacao
nodes.norm_label: constitution principle i: modularidade por chave de ativacao
nodes.rationale: NON-NEGOTIABLE: every capability is an activation flag; the matrix is the explicit expression of this principle in test form — each fixture asserts that a flag does what it claims, and the DEPENDS_ON rule enforces that a disabled parent disables its children.

nodes.label: Constitution Principle IV: Binding Duplo de Configuracao Externalizada
nodes.norm_label: constitution principle iv: binding duplo de configuracao externalizada
nodes.rationale: The binding-properties scenario explicitly provides one fixture per sub-module (default, list, map, mutable, validated) so the immutable and mutable variants are exercised independently — the auditable surface for this principle.

nodes.label: Constitution Principle VI: Validar Antes de Culpar o Codigo
nodes.norm_label: constitution principle vi: validar antes de culpar o codigo
nodes.rationale: The feature is explicitly designed to run after a clean local install of the archetype; the suite assumes the cache is fresh — a dirty cache is a known environmental issue, not a feature failure mode.

nodes.label: Regression-bait manual check
nodes.rationale: Kept manual because automation would require mutating production source (archetype-post-generate.groovy) and a failed restore would leave the archetype broken; the full matrix provides equivalent implicit coverage — any regression in the post-processor breaks every fixture.

nodes.label: Manual fixture curation (dependency rule per fixture)
nodes.norm_label: manual fixture curation (dependency rule per fixture)
nodes.rationale: Manual curation keeps fixtures readable; the archetype itself rejects semantically invalid combinations (unknown properties cause generation failure), providing a natural safety net; programmatic matrix generation from DEPENDS_ON comments is possible future work but was out of scope.

nodes.label: FR-004 dependency rule (parent off means children not exercised)
nodes.norm_label: fr-004 dependency rule (parent off means children not exercised)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the matrix free of semantically invalid combinations: when a parent flag is false, the related child flags are not exercised in that fixture (the DEPENDS_ON rule encoded in property-*.xml).

nodes.label: FR-007 offline-runnable constraint (no network/Git/Docker calls)
nodes.rationale: Tests must remain deterministic and offline-runnable once the archetype and its dependencies are cached; verify.groovy must perform no network calls, so a future edit introducing one fails the offline check.

nodes.label: FR-009 clean local install assumption
nodes.rationale: An outdated local cache cannot mask a real regression — the suite assumes a clean local install before each run (Constitution Principle VI: validate before blaming the code).

nodes.label: FR-012 security+observability exclusion (historical)
nodes.rationale: JWT + Logback + cPanel/ELK combinations were excluded so they could be addressed in a separate future assessment; historically the full/ fixture now exercises exactly that combination (all flags on), so the exclusion no longer describes the matrix.

nodes.label: T030-T032 manual validation checklist (outside the automated suite)
nodes.norm_label: t030-t032 manual validation checklist (outside the automated suite)
nodes.rationale: Regression-bait, offline-runnable and dependency-rule checks stay manual: automation would require mutating production source or a fixture that intentionally violates FR-004; the existing fixtures prove the dependency rule by induction — none combine parent=false with a child holding a non-default value.

nodes.label: BuildArtifactsTest 1.4 (monolith guard)

nodes.label: Composer Manifest (List<String> SECTIONS)

nodes.label: Decision 4: alphabetical file order via listFiles().sort
nodes.norm_label: decision 4: alphabetical file order via listfiles().sort
nodes.rationale: File.listFiles().sort { it.name } is equivalent to ls -1 | sort (lexicographic ASCII); an explicit name list would make the composer fragile to any new file added out of order, and semantic-priority ordering adds subjective decisions without clear gain.

nodes.label: Decision 2: pinning Groovy 4.0.28 via plugin <dependencies>
nodes.rationale: Plugin <dependencies> is the standard Maven3 mechanism and adds to the classpath rather than replacing it, so an exclusion is only needed if a conflict appears; empirically gmaven 2.1.1 ran with its default Groovy 2.4.9 and the composer still worked.

nodes.label: Decision 3: two separate import-stripping patterns
nodes.rationale: Separating the pure-import pattern from the commented-import pattern and processing them sequentially is more readable than replicating the POSIX compound regex; the Groovy whitespace class is semantically equivalent to the POSIX space class for ASCII.

nodes.label: Decision 7: remove the committed archetype-post-generate.groovy monolith
nodes.norm_label: decision 7: remove the committed archetype-post-generate.groovy monolith
nodes.rationale: Keeping the monolith versioned would make it a divergent source of truth from the build — exactly the anti-pattern the spec avoids; remove it only after byte-equivalence is validated by diff, and investigate any divergence before removing.

nodes.label: Decision 5: generate into target/classes/META-INF/
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the existing strategy for the generated archetype-metadata.xml (excluded from src/main/resources, packaged from target/classes); generating into src/main would mix artifact with source and couple the build to .gitignore configuration.

nodes.label: Decision 1: process-resources phase for composer invocation
nodes.norm_label: decision 1: process-resources phase for composer invocation
nodes.rationale: process-resources comes immediately after generate-resources (where xml-maven-plugin:transform assembles archetype-metadata.xml) and before package/integration-test — the same site the internal precedent occupies, guaranteeing symmetry; mixing two transformers in generate-resources would be confusing.

nodes.label: Rename: SnippetComposer to ArchetypePostGenerateComposer

nodes.label: FR-006: SECTIONS as a single readable literal data structure
nodes.norm_label: fr-006: sections as a single readable literal data structure
nodes.rationale: The order configuration MUST live in one List<String> at the top of the composer with a short comment per item — a single auditable source of truth for assembly order instead of order scattered across the code.

nodes.label: FR-007: SNIPPET-NN marker convention (flag coupling)

nodes.label: Hard Stop Message Contract (10 fields)
nodes.rationale: One normative message format for every stop and confirmation so a beginner operator can answer the 5 orientation questions (what happened, where, options, recommendation, how to resume); 10 ordered fields, 20-word sentences, 2-3 concrete options, dictionary reference, no Maven output.

nodes.label: STOP-DER-02 — Invalid Derived Attribute List
nodes.rationale: An invalid final attribute list must stop the procedure instead of falling back to String:name, because the fallback produced a plausible-but-wrong module; the message offers exactly 3 options and emits no Maven command, yielding 0 modules.

nodes.label: Stop Registry (16 stops + 2 confirmations)
nodes.rationale: The registry lives centrally in prompt-00 §0.5 while stop sites only cite the code; this lets the build fail when a stop lacks a code, a code is unregistered, or a message is missing, preventing silent stops.

nodes.label: CatalogSyncContractTest
nodes.rationale: Build-time suite proving the 3-column table, 9 defaults and 3 literal regexes in regras-04 §3.1 still match the built catalog, so catalog/procedure divergence cannot pass silently.

nodes.label: HardStopContractTest
nodes.rationale: Build-time Groovy suite that scans the 13 Markdown files for the 18 codes, 1:1 messages, 10 fields, dictionary terms, 20-word sentences, forbidden phrases and secret patterns; it fails when a stop is added without a code or a site loses its code.

nodes.label: Append-Only Convergence Contract
nodes.rationale: Converge NEVER modifies spec.md, plan.md, or rewrites tasks.md. Only appends a new '## Phase N: Convergence' section with zero-padded T{M+1:03d} IDs, ordered CRITICAL/HIGH first. On zero findings, tasks.md is left byte-for-byte unchanged.

nodes.label: Unit Tests for English (Checklist Philosophy)
nodes.rationale: Checklists validate requirements QUALITY (completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, coverage, edge cases), never implementation behavior. Required patterns: 'Are [requirement type] defined...?' / 'Is [vague term] quantified...?'. Prohibited: 'Verify', 'Test', 'Confirm' + system behavior.

nodes.label: Constitution Authority Principle
nodes.rationale: Project constitution (.specify/memory/constitution.md) is non-negotiable within analyze/converge scope. Constitution conflicts are automatically CRITICAL and require spec/plan/tasks adjustment, never dilution of the principle. Unfilled templates are skipped gracefully.

nodes.label: Extension Hooks Protocol
nodes.rationale: Reads .specify/extensions.yml; honors hooks.before_<cmd> and hooks.after_<cmd>. Filters out hooks where enabled=false; does not interpret hook condition expressions (deferred to HookExecutor). Mandatory hooks (optional:false) MUST be invoked; optional hooks surfaced with a prompt. No-silent-skip on parse errors.

nodes.label: Handoff Metadata in YAML Frontmatter
nodes.rationale: Frontmatter 'handoffs:' list declares next-stage commands (label, agent, prompt, optional send:true). Used by /speckit.specify → speckit.plan/clarify, /speckit.plan → speckit.tasks/checklist, /speckit.tasks → speckit.analyze/implement.

nodes.label: [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] Marker Convention
nodes.rationale: Hard cap of 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers per spec; prioritized by scope > security/privacy > UX > technical. Used as honest placeholder for guesses that have multiple reasonable interpretations with different implications.

nodes.label: Path Safety / Ancestor Symlink Resolution
nodes.rationale: Before any read/write, resolves the real (symlink-stripped) path of every ancestor (e.g. .specify, .specify/assessments/<slug>) and refuses if any component is a symlink or escapes the project root. Blocks a cloned or crafted project from redirecting I/O outside the repo.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure of Artifacts
nodes.rationale: Analyze/converge/clarify load only minimal necessary sections (e.g. Functional Requirements, Success Criteria from spec; Architecture/Phases from plan) instead of dumping raw artifacts. Caps analyze output at 50 findings rows.

nodes.label: Severity Heuristic Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Four-tier heuristic shared across analyze and converge: CRITICAL (constitution MUST violation, blocking baseline), HIGH (duplicate/conflicting req, ambiguous NFR, untestable acceptance), MEDIUM (terminology drift, missing NFR coverage), LOW (style/minor redundancy).

nodes.label: Slug Normalization & Safety
nodes.rationale: Normalize slugs to lowercase + [a-z0-9-] only (strip '.', '/', '\'); collapse repeated '-'; reject empty results. Guarantees the constructed ASSESS_DIR cannot escape its parent directory.

nodes.label: Spec Kit Template Resolution Stack
nodes.rationale: Project overrides compose with preset layers and extension layers above a core template fallback. Resolved at command time via .specify/scripts/powershell/resolve-template.ps1. Spec/plan/constitution/tasks templates resolved independently.

nodes.label: URL Trust Policy
nodes.rationale: Classifies hosts/schemes as refuse-outright (loopback, RFC1918, metadata endpoints) vs allowlisted public sources vs unrecognized. Defeats DNS rebinding by requiring connection-pinning to validated public addresses.

nodes.label: User-Story-Organized Task Phases
nodes.rationale: Tasks organized by user story (P1/P2/P3 from spec.md) with strict checklist format: '- [ ] [TaskID] [P?] [Story?] Description with file path'. Phase structure: Setup → Foundational → User Stories → Polish. Independent test criteria per story.

nodes.label: Decision Verdict Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Three verdicts: 'go' (problem validity adequate+, evidence strength adequate+, concept option recommended); 'needs-clarification' (promising but blocked on unknowns — name the stage to revisit); 'kill' (decisive reason stated plainly). Weak/unknown evidence forbids a go.

nodes.label: Three-Slot Packaged Archetype JAR
nodes.rationale: The Maven archetype packaging separates declaration (metadata), content (templates) and post-generation adjustment (Groovy) into three fixed JAR slots so the descriptor stays small and reviewable while never being parsed together with the template material.

nodes.label: archetype-post-generate.groovy (Post-Processor)
nodes.rationale: The metadata descriptor is static and cannot express conditional fileSets, so the Groovy post-generator exists to decide keep/delete/rename by flag on the already generated tree, without being able to add to the contract.

nodes.label: ProcedureInvariant (19 files / 13 MD / 6 JSON / 4 subfolders / 35-18 catalog)
nodes.norm_label: procedureinvariant (19 files / 13 md / 6 json / 4 subfolders / 35-18 catalog)
nodes.rationale: File counts, subfolder counts and catalog counts are frozen so a rename cannot silently add, remove or move files.

nodes.label: RenamedFile (008)
nodes.rationale: Each renamed file keeps old_name, new_name, subfolder, role, has_old_references and baseline_hash so the diff can prove that only reference tokens changed.

nodes.label: RenameManifest (008)
nodes.rationale: A single manifest of 12 mappings, short-token map, reference inventory and exclusions avoids divergent substitutions and makes the scope auditable before editing.

nodes.label: FileRenameContractTest
nodes.rationale: New Groovy contract suite that proves the 12 new names, 0 old names, 19/13/6/4 counts, index contents, catalogue 35/18 and absence of old references in the operational corpus; manual review alone was rejected because it does not fail the build.

nodes.label: Phased Rename Manifest (009)
nodes.rationale: Extends the single manifest with a phase per mapping and per reference so the rename can be delivered and demonstrated in two independent slices (03 then 04 + README).

nodes.label: FeaturePhase (009)
nodes.rationale: Splits work into Phase 1 (subfolder 03 and its references, README untouched) and Phase 2 (subfolder 04, README for both, final scan) so each phase has a demonstrable result without depending on the next.

nodes.label: RenamedFile (009, phase-aware)
nodes.rationale: Adds a phase field to the 008 RenamedFile so the contract suite can assert Phase 1 and Phase 2 states of the same 12 mappings.

nodes.label: Legacy Redirect (prompt-00 path)
nodes.rationale: The only file allowed to keep an old name: src/main/resources/utils/01-entrada-inicializacao/prompt-00-leia-este-arquivo-primeiro.md stays in place and points to 00-entry-point.md so prior specs that reference the old path keep working; no additional redirects exist.

nodes.label: PackagedProcedure (19 files; 2 in 01, 5 in 02)
nodes.rationale: The whole packaged procedure keeps 19 files (13 Markdown, 6 JSON) in 4 subfolders, with 2 files in 01 and 5 in 02, plus a 35-property/18-fileset catalogue; these counts must hold in every phase.

nodes.label: Entry Point Rename (00-entry-point.md / 01-mapa...)
nodes.rationale: prompt-00-leia-este-arquivo-primeiro.md becomes 00-entry-point.md and indice-01-mapa-dos-arquivos-e-ordem-de-leitura.md becomes 01-mapa-dos-arquivos-e-ordem-de-leitura.md, removing prompt-/indice- prefixes so numbering matches the subfolder convention; the entry point stays prompt-00 in role and needs no redirect beyond the legacy one.

nodes.label: ProcedureEntryRenameContractTest
nodes.rationale: New phase-aware Groovy suite for the 7 entry/operation names, the 19-path index, the legacy redirect and the anti-drift scan; registered in the runner so missing registration fails CoverageRegistryTest/ReadmeConsistencyTest.

nodes.label: Anti-drift Reference Scan
nodes.rationale: Scan the operational corpus (procedure, README, test suites) for regras-0[1-6] and template-0[1-6] while excluding specs/, graphify-out/, target/ and the suite itself, because historical specs and generated output are not operational sources.

nodes.label: Prefix Removal (regras-/template-)
nodes.rationale: Current names repeat the subfolder role in a prefix and delay the numeral that controls ordering; removing the prefix aligns file names with the numbered subfolder convention without changing normative content.

nodes.label: Operational Reference Update (whole corpus)
nodes.rationale: All operational references, including those inside the 12 renamed files, must be updated; historical specs, plans/tasks and generated output are explicitly excluded so only the live corpus changes.

nodes.label: Phase-aware Contract Harness
nodes.rationale: The suite infers the phase from the existence of 04-referencia-templates-de-contrato/01-schema-do-contrato.json, expecting old 04 names in Phase 1 and only new names in Phase 2, so a single suite can guard both intermediate and final states.
